PowerPoint slides with officer

Source: R/office.R
phw_pptx.Rd

phw_pptx() starts a PowerPoint deck, from the PHW template (16:9, Ubuntu text, navy titles) or from your own. phw_add_slide() adds a slide with a PHW-styled title and a chart, table or text, so a set of results becomes a deck in a few lines. Charts are added as editable vector graphics when the rvg package is installed, so colleagues can tweak them in PowerPoint.

Usage

phw_pptx(template = NULL)

phw_add_slide(
  x,
  title = NULL,
  plot = NULL,
  table = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  layout = "Title and Content",
  master = NULL,
  editable = TRUE,
  title_size = 28,
  caption_args = list(),
  alt = NULL,
  plot_scale = 1.5,
  table_fit = TRUE
)

Arguments

template

Path to a .pptx template, e.g. the PHW corporate template. NULL uses the PHW template from phw_reference_pptx().

x

An rpptx object from phw_pptx().

title

Slide title.

plot

A ggplot (or anything officer::ph_with() accepts as a graphic).

table

A data frame, flextable or summary table (rendered with phw_flextable()).

text

Character vector of bullet points.

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and shown at the bottom.

layout, master

Slide layout and slide master names in the template. A slide master is the set of layouts a template provides; see them in PowerPoint under View > Slide Master, or with officer::layout_summary(x). The default layout suits the PHW template, which also has "Title Slide" (the title and text as a subtitle), "Section Header", "Two Content", "Title Only" and "Blank". With your own template, give the layout names it uses. The default master = NULL uses the master in the deck that has the layout (the first one, if several do), so you only need master when two masters share a layout name.

editable

Add charts as editable vector graphics (needs rvg)?

title_size

Title font size. On a layout with a dark background (the title slide and section header) the template sets the size and colour, and this applies only when you give it.

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments.

alt

Alternative text for the chart or table on the slide, read out by screen readers. NULL adds none, except that a ggplot's own labs(alt = ) text is used when there is one.

plot_scale

How much to enlarge a chart's text on the slide, as a multiple of the size the chart already uses. The default 1.5 brings axis and legend text to about 14 points, which reads from the back of a room. 1 leaves the chart as it is. It scales the text and legend keys that follow the plot's base size, as theme_phw() and the ggplot2 themes do, and the size of text drawn by geom_text() with ggplot2 4.0.0 or later. Text you gave an exact size in your own theme() keeps it.

table_fit

Enlarge a table built here from a data frame or summary table so it fills the width of the slide's content area? The text grows with it, by up to 1.6 times, and a narrow table is widened by at most another 80% (more for a table with more columns). A tall table tightens its row spacing so the text can grow. FALSE keeps the table at the size phw_flextable() gives it. A flextable you pass in is never resized.

Value

An officer rpptx object. Save it with print(deck, target = "file.pptx").

Examples

if (requireNamespace("officer", quietly = TRUE)) {
  deck <- phw_pptx()
  deck <- phw_add_slide(deck, "Key messages",
                        text = c("Point one", "Point two"))
  if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point()
    deck <- phw_add_slide(deck, "A chart", plot = p, source = "mtcars", editable = FALSE)
  }
  print(deck, target = tempfile(fileext = ".pptx"))
}
